title: File BL-28: every caption is stored three times
body:
Files **BL-28**. Evidence only — **the approval is a separate pull request**, because the `plan` check's uncapped exemption covers `docs/BACKLOG.md` but not `docs/BACKLOG.approved.md`, so carrying both here would fall back to the 50-line cap. BL-28 lands in `## Proposed` and is **not** approved by this change.

**Measured across the whole cached corpus, not estimated.** 285 of 285 transcripts carry roughly three copies of every spoken word:

| | characters |
| --- | --- |
| stored in `data/transcripts/` | 38,767,230 |
| actual speech | 13,645,734 |
| **ratio** | **2.84x** |

2.54x to 3.00x per video, median 2.96x. **Not one video escapes it.**

**The mechanism.** YouTube's automatic captions use a **roll-up** presentation — two lines scroll on screen, and the track emits a cue for every *display frame* rather than for every line of speech. Every line appears three times: alone, as the tail of the previous frame, as the head of the next. Of 4,430 cues in one video, 50% extend the previous cue, 49% are a suffix of it, and 50% start within 0.02s of it. The structure is exact.

`parse_vtt` is not defective. It keeps every cue, which is correct for an ordinary WebVTT and wrong for a roll-up one.

**Why no gate saw it.** `tests/fixtures/captions_vtt.txt` — the only WebVTT the suite has ever parsed — has clean, non-overlapping cues. YouTube has never sent this project captions shaped like that fixture. That is **ESC-21 repeating exactly**: the fixture agreed with the code and both disagreed with what yt-dlp returns.

**Confirmed against the source, not argued.** The same caption track fetched in both offered formats:

| | characters | words |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `vtt`, as stored today | 217,427 | 40,966 |
| `json3`, every segment concatenated | 73,159 | 13,791 |

Four videos checked, all 2.97x–3.00x, all offering `json3`.

**The second cost is not money.** R5 cuts every excerpt window from a mention's `start_seconds`, and V11/V14 make that timestamp the thing the owner acts on. In roll-up VTT a board name inside a two-line frame inherits the **first** line's timestamp — up to ~2.5 seconds early. `json3` carries per-word offsets on 72% of segments.

**Direction recorded in the item, the owner's:** prefer `json3`; keep VTT as a fallback with de-duplication; and the fallback must **announce itself loudly**, per video and in the summary, so two provenance classes never sit in one cache with nothing to tell them apart.

One correction worth carrying forward: `aAppend` events must be **kept** — they hold real speech, and dropping them loses 2,257 words on the measured video.

No code, no design amendment, no approval. The approval, the decision and the plan each follow on their own pull requests, in that order.
